data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Z^d is amenable; random 3-regular graphs are expanders where no curvature theorem holds","asynchronous single-site updates on sparse degree-3 graphs have different fluctuation scales"],"overturn_conditions":["simulation showing positive trap frequency at large n","proof that interface length at freeze time is linear in n on expanders"],"shared_structure":["monotone energy, terminal states = local maxima","late-stage dynamics dominated by sparse, shrinking defect structure"],"source_memory_refs":["voter-model / majority coarsening on Z^d and on trees: interfaces shrink by curvature and consensus is reached","random greedy annihilation of finite defects in low-density regimes"],"transfer_claims":["late-stage sparse interfaces get annihilated rather than crystallized into matching cuts"]},"claim":"As n grows, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to 1. The obstruction structures are the locally stable mixed configurations where crossing edges form a matching (each vertex has at most one opposite-color neighbor), equivalently both color classes induce subgraphs of minimum degree >= 2. But these are exponentially rare among REACHABLE states of the dynamics: the coarsening process preferentially shrinks interfaces, and a matching cut requires a global, low-entropy conspiracy. Quantitative law: the probability that the dynamics ever visits a stable mixed configuration is at most exp(-c' n) for some c' > 0, hence consensus probability = 1 - exp(-c' n) -> 1, as n grows to infinity.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If interface length stays Theta(n) at freeze time on the expander (no curvature-driven shrinkage because the graph is non-amenable), the annihilation-stage argument fails and consensus could be unlikely.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the number of surviving interface components at the final stage is linear in n, the per-arc trap probabilities sum to a constant and consensus probability is strictly between 0 and 1.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If there exists a positive-density family of trap configurations with per-trap basin probability not exponentially small, the claim fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Energy = monochromatic edges is strictly increasing under unstable updates; there are at most 3n/2 energy values, so the dynamics terminates in O(n) increases interleaved with neutral shuffles. Termination happens at a stable state; stable states are matching cuts. The probability of ending at a mixed stable state equals the probability that, at the final coarsening stage, the surviving interface (which is whp a collection of short disconnected arcs, each an induced path whose endpoints would need to be simultaneously stabilized) closes into a matching rather than being ground away. The final stage is dominated by boundary annihilation: an induced path interface shrinks at its endpoints; to freeze it must instead wrap into cycles on both sides, an event requiring two simultaneous induced 2-cores of opposite color closing around each other \u2014 probability exp(-Theta(n)) per surviving arc and only O(log n) arcs survive to the final stage by a martingale argument on interface length, giving exp(-c' n) total trap probability. Hence whp consensus.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
